Paseo integration is currently Linux-only for managed process ownership checks
(`.pi/lib/tools/paseo-setup.ts`, adapted by `extensions/paseo/extension.ts`). New launches default to loopback and use
per-user state under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pi-swarm/paseo` (default
`~/.local/state/pi-swarm/paseo`). Existing owned PID records are checked before
launch, subprocesses are bounded, and daemon health includes HTTP validation.
`/paseo setup inspect` only inspects Tailscale. Explicit `/paseo setup apply` (or a tool
setup call with `apply: true`) discovers the machine hostname, merges `daemon.hostnames`,
hot-reloads the daemon, and creates an unoccupied persistent tailnet-only Serve
route. Session startup only starts/checks the daemon, never changes network
exposure. `/paseo setup apply` retries the same operation. Existing conflicting routes or
Funnel exposure fail closed; matching routes are reverified without replacement.
Success requires HTTPS health plus a WebSocket hello/status/pong handshake.
`PASEO_HOME` is injected into managed launches. Config writes are atomic and mode
0600, anchored to verified Linux directory descriptors; setup/start/stop/update/build
share a lock. Update/build refuse live daemon records; stop retains records until
termination is verified. Interrupted locks require inspection, not age-only
automatic stealing. This is not yet an unattended cross-platform
installer or boot-time service. Fresh global package clones do not include a
built Paseo submodule. Validate with `npx vitest run .pi/test/tools/paseo.test.ts`;
those tests do not prove process supervision or cross-device connectivity.

The PageIndex-style context adapter registers `context_index`, `context_remember`,
`context_reindex`, `context_search`, `context_outline`, `context_read`,
`context_inspect`, and `context_delete`; these are retained by the default tool
surface. Session reload accepts Pi custom-entry envelopes. Retrieval consultations
use tool-disabled Pi subprocesses; selected sections are materialized by the
parent. `context-consult.ts` limits elapsed time and accepted output, but Pi's
exec API buffers child output internally (peak memory is not streaming-bounded).
The context index still has session scope; cross-session knowledge integration
is unfinished. `.pi/lib/state/knowledge-store.ts` and
`.pi/lib/context/knowledge-capture.ts` are tested integration components. Bootstrap now uses
`knowledge-recall.ts` to project verified durable records into cited PageIndex
reads; candidate records are excluded, storage failure is distinct from no match,
and recall now ranks all current scoped records from a single event-log projection before applying the response cap. `memory_history` supports `get` by scoped ID and status-filtered search for
candidate review. Review instructions require source evidence and later
corrections before revision-checked verification; extraction alone is not proof.
New non-session `memory_history` writes now use this store; legacy records remain
readable and labeled unverified. Correction/deletion require revision checks.
Agent global writes fail closed. `/memory-promote repository|worktree ID [namespace]`
requires interactive confirmation of a verified record and rechecks its revision
before making an explicitly approved global copy; the project record stays intact. Lifecycle candidate capture is registered in `knowledge-enrichment.ts`: on
`agent_settled` and `session_before_compact`, it processes new visible evidence,
persists a `pi-swarm-knowledge-enrichment` cursor, and saves cited candidates.
It excludes reasoning/runtime reminders and suppresses child-agent capture.
`/memory-capture on|off|status` controls this per session;
`PI_SWARM_MEMORY_CAPTURE=off` disables it initially. Consultations are awaited
and may add up to their timeout to turn completion. `candidate-memory-review.ts`
reviews at most one pending record per settled turn (or `/memory-review`) using
`PI_SWARM_MEMORY_REVIEW_MODEL` (default `clover-plexus/luna`). It reads only cited
Pi session entries, requires a bounded model verdict with a source-matching
quote, and corrects the existing record by exact revision; failed review leaves
it candidate. This is a model judgment, not independent proof, and it never
writes global scope. `task-candidate-capture.ts` projects TaskManage's current
task snapshot into worktree-scoped candidates: each record includes every task
question, answered or unanswered, plus answer/evidence when present. Repeated
snapshots are idempotent and changed answers create revisions; the per-task
record is never verified. In addition, each answer of a *completed* task becomes
its own `kind: fact` record (source `taskmanage-answer:<session>:<task>:<question>`,
text `Q:/A:/Task:`). `.pi/lib/state/answer-evidence.ts` anchors its evidence at
capture: `path#Lx-Ly` stores the redacted span text, `file.md#Heading` the
heading line, `tool:Name#n` the cited session entry (`<session>.jsonl#<id>`) and
a result excerpt, and a bare path is existence-only. The record is `verified`
iff at least one anchored ref exists and every ref resolved; otherwise it stays
candidate with the unresolved refs and reasons in its text. Anchors are frozen at
first capture. Paths are stored relative to, and bounded by, the git worktree
root (the same identity that keys the worktree store), so recall from any
subdirectory re-checks the same file; other worktrees do not see these records.
`recallKnowledge` (bootstrap) re-checks file spans/headings of
answer records on every read and drops changed ones as `staleExcluded`.
"Verified" here means the cited evidence is unchanged, not that the answer is
correct. E2E: `node tools/e2e/taskmanage-answer-memory.mjs` (real Pi, scripted
provider; 9 steps including subdirectory recall, uncited-edit near miss and cited-edit stale).
Unverified candidates remain excluded from bootstrap recall. `context_search` can report candidate-leads on a session
index miss, with Q&A projected as Markdown sections rather than raw JSON.
`memory_history` operation `recall` invokes a bounded read-only memory agent
using `PI_SWARM_MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_MODEL` or the session model (Luna fallback),
and returns selected source cards, not the child agent's prose. The sibling
`memory_history` operation `ask` uses the same scoped PageIndex projection and
isolated browse/read/select child, but requires the child to submit a bounded
answer citing its read/selected card keys. The parent validates the receipt
and returns the answer alongside original record IDs, revisions, statuses and
citations. An empty index or unsupported answer returns no answer; a failed or
malformed child is reported distinctly. Candidate cards remain unverified
leads; `ask` neither writes nor changes bootstrap's verified-only recall.
When the isolated child submits a receipt but later exits nonzero or times out,
the parent still validates that committed receipt; without one, it returns
`unavailable`. Abort and session-generation checks still reject stale results.
The `ask`/`recall` model-visible text now leads with outcome and answer (or
explicit no-answer), then bounded source-card IDs, status, excerpts and
citations; structured `details` retain the full prior retrieval result.
Other memory operations retain their JSON text. The tool's TUI-only renderer
shows a compact outcome/answer and an expanded source view without repeating
the raw JSON or changing retrieval state. Reload to update an active session.
The opt-in synthetic `live-answer.mjs` run enables child-only metadata tracing
(`PI_SWARM_MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_TRACE=1`) and saves offered cards, ordered
browse/read/select events, receipt, exit and final tool response under ignored
`artifacts/memory-retrieval/live-answer-*/results.jsonl`. Normal retrieval
does not emit these traces; they are not added to model-visible results.
`offer` lets the main agent hand explicit “remember that” content to a
tool-less reviewer for a durable candidate and indexed acknowledgment. Existing
`get` and other write operations retain their contracts. `search` now accepts
reordered queries when every distinctive term occurs in the same record (as
well as exact phrase matches); it does not synonym-expand or automatically
include another scope. `recall` ranks strict PageIndex section matches first
and fills unused candidate slots with partial matches containing at least two
distinctive terms; the read-only agent still decides whether they support the
query. A typo or synonym without lexical overlap may still return no result.
Historical backlog review is incremental. Store path checks reject
existing symlinks; hostile concurrent ancestor replacement is outside its current
filesystem guarantees. No live backfill is implied by these library tests.

Memory/skill semantics are shared in `.pi/lib/context/memory-guidance.ts`.
Memory stores project/domain knowledge, decisions and rationale, preferences,
and contextual facts (including how a project operates); skills store reusable
agent procedures. Mixed observations must be separated, not copied wholesale.
Repository is the shared-memory default; worktree holds unmerged facts, session
holds local context, and global requires explicitly shareable cross-project
knowledge. Do not automatically duplicate facts across scopes. The PageIndex-style
context extension currently retains its namespace/workspace/session boundary.

Bootstrap selects at most two distinct skills (preferring one), enforces the cap
in selector validation and orchestration, and invokes them before task drafting.
The planner receives bounded, explicitly truncated instruction excerpts; the
main agent receives up to 12,000 characters per skill with explicit truncation
and an exact full-output spill file for further reads, without another invocation.
This preview limit does not cap orchestrator tool calls or continued investigation.

Bootstrap shared-memory recall uses task-token ranking across text and tags before
its candidate cap (`recallShared`); explicit memory search retains substring
semantics. Bootstrap handoff asks for evidence-backed knowledge enrichment after
verification, not automatic transcript ingestion. No new learning is a valid
outcome. Historical backfills must be reviewed, scoped, and redacted before
promotion; experimental stores use `PI_SWARM_MEMORY_DIR`.

`/mem on|off|status` persists bootstrap enforcement per repository. On adds a
memory ceremony to the final assembled system prompt and blocks ordinary tool
calls until bootstrap succeeds in the current session. Bootstrap and user/plan
interaction remain available; `/mem off` is the recovery escape. Bootstrap is
exempt from skill-budget gates, but selected skills still require real invocation
to activate the working budget. Reload resets readiness, not the persisted mode.

## Package boundaries

- `packages/context/prompt` owns prompt precedence, workspace context, and non-secret
  provenance; chain `event.systemPrompt` instead of overwriting blindly.
- `packages/policy/policy` owns final fail-closed authorization. Tool registration or a prompt
  instruction is not authorization.
- `packages/tools/taskmanage`, `packages/tools/agents`, `history-search`, and `memory-history` own their
  respective durable workflows; use stable IDs and bounded outputs.
- `packages/runtime/core` owns shared runtime identity/lifecycle; extensions must not each
  invent global identity or duplicate lifecycle state.
- `packages/context/skills`, `packages/context/autogenskills`, `packages/tools/mcp`, and `packages/tools/schedule` provide opt-in capability
  layers; do not make ambient discovery silently widen a closed profile.
- `packages/runtime/contract` and `packages/runtime/runtime-contracts` define interfaces consumed by
  multiple packages; change them deliberately and update all consumers/tests.
- Import direction is fixed by who runs the code. `.pi/` imports package
  sources by relative path (`../../../packages/<layer>/<name>/src/index.ts`):
  Pi loads extensions through jiti with plain Node resolution and no build
  step, so a bare `@pi-swarm/<name>` import there would silently depend on a
  stale or missing `dist/`. Package-to-package imports use the bare workspace
  name (`@pi-swarm/core`, `@pi-swarm/runtime-contracts`) against that
  package's `dist` exports so `tsc` `rootDir` boundaries hold. Do not mix the
  two; `tools/repo/rewrite-imports.mjs --check` verifies the relative side.

## Change contract

Every agent must:

1. Read this file and inspect `git status --short` before editing.
2. Create/update a TaskManage task for multi-step work and keep its status
   current.
3. Identify the owning package/extension before changing code; avoid unrelated
   refactors and preserve existing user changes.
4. Update this file's index, inventory, package boundaries, or flow whenever
   files, ownership, commands, extension registration, or architecture change.
5. Add focused tests for behavior changes where practical, and document any
   intentional test gap.
6. Report files changed, validation run, and known limitations.

When adding a new top-level package, extension, persistent entry type, hook
group, or user-facing command, add it to the relevant tables above in the same
patch. This is a contract, not optional documentation.

```sh

npm run build                     # tsc for every package, dependency order
npm test                          # vitest: packages/**/test, .pi/test, tests/
npx vitest run .pi/test/context   # one layer, or any path/file
```

### Installing globally

The repository is itself a Pi package (root `package.json` `pi` manifest:
individual extension entrypoints and `.pi/themes`). Never copy `extensions/`
anywhere — the extensions import `.pi/lib` and `packages/*/src` by relative
path (tests import `tests/fixtures`) and need the hoisted `node_modules`.

```sh
# dev box: link this checkout (no copy; dedupes against .pi/ by absolute path)
pi install /home/swarm/Work/Pi-Swarm
# any other machine (pin a tag or commit; `pi update` reconciles the ref)
pi install git:github.com/cloverinternational/trebol@<tag>
# from the installed checkout: PATH, versions, dist, deps, models.json, theme, packages[]
npm run doctor
```

What `pi install` does (vendor/pi-mono `package-manager.ts`): `git clone`
(no submodules) into `~/.pi/agent/git/<host>/<path>`, then
`npm install --omit=dev`, never `npm run build`. Consequences that are
contracts here:

- the root `prepare` script is the only build a global install gets; every
  package consumed from `dist/` at runtime (`@pi-swarm/core`,
  `@pi-swarm/runtime-contracts`) must be in `build:runtime`;
- anything imported at runtime is in root or package `dependencies`, never
  `devDependencies`;
- nothing under `vendor/` is imported at runtime (submodules are empty in a
  package clone); `ask_user_question` is the in-tree fork for that reason;
- on a machine that also opens this repo as a project, use the local-path
  form — a `git:` install has a different absolute path and would register
  every tool twice.

Prove a change against the package path, not just the project boot.
Host-level items (node on the
non-interactive `PATH`, `models.json` `maxTokens`, tmux launch shell,
provider key scope) are outside the package; `npm run doctor` reports the
first two.

Run the narrowest relevant check first, then broader checks when the change is
cross-package. Never claim a check passed unless it was actually run. After
moving files, run the import rewriter with a move map and then `--check`
rather than editing specifiers by hand.

## Safety and vendor policy

- Preserve uncommitted user changes. Never reset, clean, or rewrite unrelated
  files.
- Do not expose credentials, API keys, session transcripts, generated state,
  or large dependency trees in source changes or output. Treat `.pi/config` as
  sensitive; use the credential vault for provided secrets.
- Do not edit, format, regenerate, delete, move, or otherwise mutate anything
  under `vendor/` (formerly `upstream/`). Read it for reference and implement
  local changes in packages, extensions, tools, or docs. If a vendored change
  appears necessary, stop and ask for explicit approval.

### Compact TaskManage completion questions

Tasks may carry 1–12 `questions: [{id,text}]` (IDs ≤64, text ≤240).
Complete them with `answers: [{question,answer,evidence}]` in the same update;
answers are ≤240 characters, evidence references ≤512. Use workspace-local
`file.md#heading` or `file#Lx-Ly` references for detailed proof. Missing answers,
unknown IDs and unavailable evidence reject completion. Reference availability
is not semantic verification. Legacy questionless tasks remain compatible.
Bootstrap carries questions into task proposals and committed operations. No
separate question lifecycle or follow-up tool-call limit is introduced.

`create` operation keys are idempotency keys (#298). A replayed key succeeds
only when the request is identical: each task stores `createFingerprint`, a
SHA-256 of its create op. A different payload fails with non-retryable
`idempotency_conflict` naming the existing task. Tasks persisted before the
fingerprint fall back to comparing subject and questions. Update keys stay
reusable per-call aliases. E2E: `node tools/e2e/taskmanage-create-key-conflict.mjs`.

## Jev first-finder knowledge audit (opt-in)

`/jev-audit on|off|status|now` controls the session audit; environment
`PI_SWARM_JEV_AUDIT=on` enables it initially. `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is resolved from the environment first, then the exact vault
credential `typesafe-api-key` through the existing internal resolver (never tool
parameters). `PI_SWARM_JEV_CREDENTIAL_ID` overrides the ID;
`PI_SWARM_JEV_VAULT=off` disables fallback. Values are never put in audit evidence. The state-layer adapter
`extensions/jev-knowledge-audit/extension.ts` counts completed Pi turns and
audits at the next turn start after five new turns, and on agent_end for final evidence. Stop audits process one bounded batch and never wake the agent; remaining backlog is retained. Domain collection/API/review
logic is in `.pi/lib/context/jev-knowledge-audit.ts`; mode coordination lives in
`jev-audit-mode.ts`. Persisted `pi-swarm-jev-audit` entries hold cursor/count and
bounded redacted pending review; `pi-swarm-jev-review` context messages are
untrusted proposals, injected once without a wake-up turn.

Jev is the first classifier, not a generator or verifier. At most three bounded
new excerpts per audit are routed as memory, procedure, mixed, temporary, unresolved,
or noise. Backlog remains for later audits. Main agent review and existing
revision-checked memory_history/SkillManage tools own all actual writes. Skills
are audited only when their visible invocation/view output is encountered; no
whole-library automatic scan or rewrite. Mandatory instructions are not removed.

Existing generative knowledge-enrichment capture defers while Jev is enabled;
off preserves its old behavior. A three-second deadline, session cancellation,
child suppression, exact citations and bounded request/response protect the loop.
API failure keeps evidence retryable and never blocks ordinary work. Missing
compacted cursors pause audit rather than guessing. `/jev-audit now` queues review
for the next model context; it does not start a new turn. Reload/new session is
required to load newly installed extension code.

Focused validation: `npx vitest run .pi/test/context/jev-knowledge-audit.test.ts
.pi/test/state/jev-knowledge-audit.test.ts .pi/test/state/knowledge-enrichment.test.ts`.
Live API test is opt-in: `PI_SWARM_JEV_LIVE_TEST=1 npx vitest run
.pi/test/context/jev-live.test.ts` with the key in the environment.

## Budgeted Jev-triggered memory maintenance

Enable `/jev-audit on` then `/memory-worker on`. `/memory-worker off|status`
controls the parent-session queue. Defaults: one worker at a time, up to four
queued Jev packets, six new child model turns, 90-second wall deadline. The main
agent remains free to work. No Harbor or global memory/skill edits are involved.

`extensions/memory-maintenance/extension.ts` owns queue/cancellation/receipts;
`.pi/lib/context/memory-maintenance-runner.ts` snapshots the active visible branch
and invokes actual Pi `--fork` into a separate child session. Snapshots are
redacted, omit reasoning, preserve source IDs, are capped at 2MB, and remain under
ignored `.pi/agent-sessions/` for evidence links. No parent branch switch occurs.
The child loads only `.pi/lib/state/memory-maintenance-worker.ts`, with no normal
extensions/tools. Its allowlist is `memory_evidence` and restricted `memory_history`.

The worker must search first, read cited snapshot evidence before verified writes,
and use expectedRevision for corrections. Repository/worktree only; global/session
writes, deletion, nested agents, shell, code edits and SkillManage are unavailable.
Verified status is attributed agent judgment, not proof from Jev. Procedure findings
remain unresolved skill proposals rather than autonomous skill edits. Cancellation
revokes a write lease and terminates the subprocess; completed prior writes remain
valid history. Interrupted/failed runs may contain partial writes: inspect before
retrying. A filesystem lease check is not a cross-process transactional barrier.

`.pi/lib/context/memory-query-budget.ts` tracks successful repository/worktree
`memory_history` search/get/replay calls by ID and result. Successful empty lookup
counts; failures, writes and other scopes/tools do not. After ten completed main
turns without lookup, one soft reminder is injected. It rearms on successful lookup
or a new interactive/RPC input; it never blocks tools or starts a new turn.

Worker completion is a bounded operation receipt at the next natural context
boundary, not an unsolicited continuation. Jev packets are reviewed by the worker
when enabled, otherwise by the main agent. Session replacement cancels stale work.
Reload may restart an interrupted queued item; store dedup/CAS limit repeated writes.

Validation: focused `memory-maintenance*` and `memory-query-budget` Vitest tests;
`node tools/experiments/jev-audit/memory-worker-smoke.mjs` exercises real installed
Pi fork/evidence/write/query against a local scripted provider and isolated store.
It does not establish unscripted reviewer accuracy or quality improvements.

### Task enforcement correction

The canonical TaskManage hook pipeline now defaults to `block`, not `off`:
acting tools require a focused in-progress task; TaskManage, planning, interaction,
skill and read-only recovery paths remain available. The secondary coordinator
stays silent to avoid duplicate hooks. Explicit hook-off policy remains honored.
`node tools/experiments/jev-audit/task-enforcement-smoke.mjs` proves actual Pi
blocked write -> TaskManage create -> successful write in a temporary workspace.
`memory_history` `search`/`get` are exempt from this gate (`isReadOnlyMemoryCall`
in `.pi/lib/runtime/swarm-toolclass.ts`); its write operations stay gated. All
hooks are dormant for the first 5 turns (`HOOK_WARMUP_TURNS`), except composition
hooks registered with `{ warmup: false }` (swarm-prompt, so the Forge prompt reaches the first
request; e2e `node tools/e2e/forge-prompt-first-turn.mjs`), so gate smokes
must pad warm-up turns: `node tools/e2e/memory-gate.mjs` does, while the
task-enforcement smoke above does not and currently passes its first write.
Reviewed, citable project facts promoted from memory candidates live in
`docs/reference/project-findings.md` under stable `F-NNNN` headings.

Supervisor operational-review settings now also control reviewed parent task
application; the hidden PI_SWARM_SUPERVISOR_TASK_APPLY flag is no longer required.
Independent confirmation, live snapshot checks and owning TaskManage hooks remain
mandatory. Project `enabled:false` still disables audit/worker, not the normal
task-enforcement hooks. Reload is required for already-running sessions.

### Durable skill-budget enforcement

Autogen `gateTool` enforcement no longer depends on `modelContext`: disabling
manager-generated prose in the Pi adapter does not disable execution gating.
In auto mode, after task focus, the durable manager charges non-exempt calls
(including Bash), blocks the next call at5 onboarding/90 working calls, and
resets through actual successful Skill invocation. SkillManage list/view alone
cannot refill this budget. Recovery/task/interaction/read tools remain exempt.
The built-in skill-budget hook now reads the durable manager's gate and status,
so its model-visible block names `Skill` and explains that `SkillManage` create,
patch, view, or review does not refill: create if appropriate, then invoke.
Read-only Bash still counts, while a blocked call is not charged. The builtin
lifecycle skill-review reminder remains separate from the execution budget;
explicit autogen manual/off modes remain distinct.
Verify real host: `node tools/experiments/jev-audit/skill-budget-smoke.mjs`.

### Human handoff on unfinished stop

ask_user_question uses the ask-user questionnaire schema and explicit submit/cancel
flow. The old timeout argument and dialog fallback are not part of this schema.
Run `npm run test:ask-user` for the extension-local Node test suite.

After observed work and a normal stop, taskmanage's canonical turn_end hook now
considers unowned pending/in-progress tasks (including blocked tasks), reconciles
actual progress, and instructs one ask_user_question call about remaining work.
A prose question alone does not replace the tool. The once-per-external-request
allowance, abort/error/user-interaction/background-work/shutdown and plan/child
suppression remain. No auto-completion, deletion, or infinite continuation.
Headless unavailable interaction must be reported with pending tasks retained.

### Bootstrap task-first recovery

Bootstrap now establishes an active task before fallible model consultation, or
reuses the existing active task. It commits validated task reconciliation by default;
legacy commitTasks is accepted but no longer disables task creation. Deterministic
request keys avoid duplicate seed tasks on retry. Model failure does not prove
bootstrap readiness; it leaves the created task and a visible error for recovery.

The memory ceremony exempts TaskManage and normalized ask_user_question/ask_user
interaction names, plus bootstrap and plan controls. Other gates still apply.
Bootstrap renderer falls back for empty details rather than printing undefined.
This renderer fix alone does not diagnose why a particular provider consultation
failed. Reload required; inspect the returned explicit bootstrap failure if it persists.

### Temporary runtime review logs
Bootstrap and Jev write bounded metadata under the active Git worktree root's
`.swarmpi/execution/` and `.swarmpi/jev/` (cwd for non-Git projects). Bootstrap
records correlated starts/stages/results/failure stage, selected memory IDs and
skills/task mappings. Jev records attempt/outcome counts, not raw evidence or
credentials. Best-effort writes must never break execution. Seven-day retention
on next write, 500 files/category, 32KiB/file. Gitignored, safe to delete; logs are
not memory and do not backfill earlier runs. Reload required for instrumentation.

### Memory capture quality, first curation batch
Lifecycle capture supplies project identity and a bounded sample of existing
records to discourage semantic duplicates. Its prompt excludes transient execution
history and asks for explicit project ownership. These are model guidance, not a
semantic enforcement guarantee. Saved candidates emit metadata receipts under
.swarmpi/execution. Restricted reviewer policy uses the same durability filter.
First code-reviewed worktree records document verified-only recall and the exact
supervisor configuration location; tools/experiments/memory-curation/save-reviewed.ts
writes them through the canonical store and checks production recall. This does not
bulk-clean existing candidates, enable supervisor, or certify unrelated records.

## Installed MCP adapter ownership

When `pi-mcp-adapter` is installed (its `/pi-mcp` command is present), it owns
`/mcp`, MCP connection negotiation, resources, and prompts. Pi-Swarm skips its
fallback startup discovery; the fallback diagnostic command is `/swarm-mcp`.
Pi-Swarm's surface filter preserves already-selected registered MCP tools,
including adapter definitions labelled `MCP:`, but does not reactivate tools
excluded by the user's selection. Adapter configs use literal `headers` (or
its explicit credential-reference syntax), not Pi-Swarm's custom `apiKey` fields.
Never print header values during diagnostics. Vendor example configs are not
runtime configuration sources.

### Install recovery diagnostics

`tools/install/doctor.mjs` checks runtime dependencies including `re2-wasm`
and all three prepare-built runtime packages. Its package-source helper
(`tools/install/package-sources.mjs`) resolves local settings paths and flags
historical Trebol/Swarm Git installs alongside a development checkout. A Git
clone is not the same resource identity as the local checkout: keep only one
registration to avoid duplicate tools. Run `npm install` in a fresh checkout
before opening Pi; local package registration alone does not prove dependencies
or dist outputs exist. Regression tests: `tests/install-package-sources.test.ts`.

Installation layout is documented in `docs/reference/install-layout.md`.
`npm run check:install` uses `tools/install/check-load.mjs` to load the package
with isolated temporary settings, without starting a session or invoking a model.
`tools/install/pi-host.mjs` resolves the SDK belonging to the PATH executable
(or `PI_EXECUTABLE`); the toggle session probe shares this resolver. No hardcoded
global npm prefix. This executes extension factories, not a security sandbox;
it does not certify individual tools or real-user resource filters.

### Flat extension migration (worktree)

Public entrypoints are `extensions/<name>/index.ts`; implementations and private
assets live beside them. Root manifest ordering is explicit for compatibility,
not a dependency injection mechanism. `control-task-tools` owns its daemon
client and registrations; `mcp-fallback` owns fallback MCP and the legacy
`/swarm-runtime` diagnostic; `swarm-agent-tools` owns both Agent/AgentControl and
legacy agent tools with one manager. Only `swarm-prompt` registers prompt hooks.
Only `vault` registers the vault tool; history does not silently enable it.
No legacy layer manifests remain. Existing user resource filters require the
path migration in `tools/repo/extension-moves.json`; personal settings are not
automatically rewritten. Shared `.pi/lib/runtime` helpers remain and are not
claimed to be eliminated by this migration.

Installation verification supports `npm run check:install -- --extension
extensions/<name>/index.ts` for isolated entry loading. The preview-only settings
migration command is `node tools/install/migrate-extension-paths.mjs
<settings.json>`; it never writes configuration and flags legacy glob filters for
manual review. See the independent-extensions architecture record for latest
verification and unresolved macOS shell / task-correction smoke failures.

Headless task correction uses the normal Pi tool_call rejection/result path;
stream-time speculative abort is TUI-only. Validation:
`.pi/test/runtime/hook-correction-headless.test.ts` and

toolsAdded.description:
Launch a background agent for long-running work that shouldn't block the conversation. Use for large-scale analysis, multi-file refactoring, or operations that may take minutes. Returns immediately with an agent_id and output_file path. Use TaskOutput(agent_id, action='result') to retrieve output, or Read the output_file directly for a live view while running. Do not duplicate the agent's work on the same files while it is running.

toolsAdded.name: DelegateOutput
toolsAdded.description:
Interact with an active delegate agent spawned by Delegate().

Actions:
  "status"  — Check current state, pending questions, and task progress.
  "poll"    — Wait up to 10s for a question from the delegate or completion.
              Use this to efficiently wait for questions without busy-looping.
  "answer"  — Send your answer to a pending question. The delegate resumes immediately.
  "result"  — Read the delegate's final output. Use offset for incremental reads.
  "cancel"  — Cancel a running delegate.

Typical polling loop:
  while true:
    out = DelegateOutput(agent_id, "poll")
    if out has question → DelegateOutput(agent_id, "answer", "your answer")
    if out.status == "done" → DelegateOutput(agent_id, "result") and break

Pass offset from a previous 'result' call to read only new content.

Codemode: `tools.DelegateOutput(args)` resolves to a string.

You normally do NOT need to pass workspace_path; it is an advanced override for pinning one exact absolute workspace. Returns bounded conversation metadata and provenance, not full transcripts. complete=false and partial_reasons mean the scan hit a resource limit or skipped malformed/oversized records; do not interpret partial results as exhaustive. Use HistoryGet only for selected conversation IDs.

toolsAdded.name: Skill

Execute a skill within the main conversation.

When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills match.
When a skill matches the user's request, this is a BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: invoke
the relevant Skill tool BEFORE generating any other response about the task.

A successful Skill invocation (not SkillManage) refills the skill tool-call budget.

Available skills are listed in system-reminder messages in the conversation.

Parameters:
  - skill: The name of the skill to invoke
  - args: Optional arguments to pass to the skill (space-separated)

The skill's instructions will be returned as the tool result. Follow them carefully.

Codemode: `tools.Skill(args)` resolves to a string.

args.description: Optional arguments to pass to the skill. Space-separated values that replace {{arg}} placeholders in the skill content.

skill.description: The name of the skill to invoke. Available skills are listed in system-reminder messages.

toolsAdded.name: SkillManage
toolsAdded.description:
Create or manage autogenerated skills. SkillManage does not invoke a skill or refill the skill tool-call budget. After creating a skill, invoke it with Skill to refill; a no-mutation review does not refill.

The target library is class-level: prefer enriching an existing umbrella skill
over creating a narrow one-session skill. Preserve specific context in a labeled
SKILL.md subsection or a references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/ support file.

Actions:
  - create: Create a new class-level umbrella only when no loaded or existing skill covers the workflow. Never overwrite an existing skill.
  - patch: Patch an existing skill immediately when you find it outdated, incomplete, or wrong — don't wait to be asked
  - write_file: Add narrow but valuable context under an existing umbrella skill
  - absorb_files: Carry support files from one skill package into another byte-for-byte. Use this when merging, NOT read_file+write_file.
  - read_file: Read one support file from an existing skill package
  - review: Record a completed review with no mutation when nothing reusable was learned
  - view: Load a skill's full instructions. When you view a skill, follow its instructions for the current task. If the skill needs updating, patch it immediately.
  - history: List immutable package revisions, newest first.
  - undo: Append a revert revision restoring a prior package state.
  - list: See all available skills with name, version, and description
  - archive: Recoverably archive a skill. Supply absorbed_into after consolidation, or pruning_reason when no knowledge was retained.

Parameters:
  - action: "create" | "patch" | "write_file" | "absorb_files" | "read_file" | "review" | "view" | "history" | "undo" | "list" | "archive"
  - name: skill identifier matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ (max 64; "archive" and Windows device aliases are reserved)
  - description: what the skill does (create, patch)
  - instructions: the full skill body (create, patch; configured policy may impose a minimum)
  - append: append patch instructions instead of replacing them
  - tags: comma-separated discovery tags (optional, create)
  - category: organization category (optional, create)
  - file_path/file_content: support file path and content (write_file)
  - from_skill: skill whose support files are being carried across (absorb_files)
  - file_paths: comma-separated support paths to carry; omit to carry every support file (absorb_files)
  - absorbed_into/pruning_reason: archive provenance; one is required
  - dropped_files: comma-separated support paths you deliberately decline to carry, with archive; each must be justified in pruning_reason or the archive is refused
  - review_reason: why no skill mutation is appropriate (review)
  - offset/limit: optional Unicode character range for paged view output
  - expected_revision: revision returned by view; required for existing-skill mutations
  - revision: optional history revision to restore (undo defaults to the prior revision)

absorb_files copies bytes on disk. Use it to preserve bytes and revision tracking when moving a script,
image, or other binary artifact between packages: read_file + write_file routes
the content through the model, which silently rewrites text and cannot represent
binary at all. archive with absorbed_into is refused when the source still has
support files the umbrella does not hold byte-for-byte.

Returns the skill path (create), updated skill info (patch), full skill content (view),
or a listing of all skills (list).

Codemode: `tools.SkillManage(args)` resolves to a string.

absorbed_into.description: Umbrella skill that absorbed this skill before archive

append.description: Append patch instructions instead of replacing them

dropped_files.description: Comma-separated support paths deliberately not carried forward; requires pruning_reason to justify the loss

expected_revision.description: Current revision returned by view; required for existing-skill mutations

file_path.description: Relative support path under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/

file_paths.description: Comma-separated support paths to carry; omit to carry every support file (absorb_files)

from_skill.description: Source skill whose support files are copied into 'name' (absorb_files)

instructions.description: Full skill body; configured policy may impose a minimum

limit.description: For view: maximum Unicode characters returned. For history: maximum revisions returned, newest first (full history when omitted).

name.description: Skill identifier; archive and Windows device aliases are reserved

offset.description: Unicode character offset for paged view output

pruning_reason.description: Why archive is safe when there is no absorption target

review_reason.description: Why the completed review needs no skill mutation

revision.description: Revision to restore (undo; defaults to prior revision)

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

toolsAdded.name: memory_history
toolsAdded.description:
Recall and enrich durable redacted memory. Use operation=ask with a natural-language query to have a read-only memory agent answer using cited scoped records; no evidence yields no answer. Use operation=recall to retrieve source cards without an answer. To pass an explicit 'remember that' request to the memory reviewer, use operation=offer with text, source and cited evidence in repository/worktree scope; it stores only a candidate and acknowledges indexing. Memory records what is known: project architecture, domain facts, terminology, decisions and rationale, constraints, preferences, and relevant ongoing context. A project's established process is knowledge about that project. Reusable instructions for how an agent should investigate, implement, debug, or verify belong in skills, not memory. Separate factual context from procedural advice when an observation contains both. Preserve evidence, uncertainty, and freshness; later corrections may invalidate earlier claims. Do not treat an agent's success claim as verified fact. Use repository scope for shared project knowledge; worktree scope for unmerged or experimental facts; session scope for local conversational context. Use global only for explicitly shareable cross-project facts or preferences, not merely because a lesson sounds reusable. Do not duplicate a fact into both repository and global scope by default. Reading combined scopes does not authorize wider writes. Search before saving to avoid duplicates. Include evidence references; exclude secrets and raw transcripts. Defaults to repository scope. Search scope all includes repository/worktree/global. Use search with status candidate to find pending knowledge, then get by id to inspect its full evidence. Review source evidence and later corrections before using correct to mark a candidate verified; leave unsupported claims pending. Writes default to candidate; verified records require evidence references (verification is an attributed claim, not automatic proof). correct/delete require id and expectedRevision. Agent tool calls cannot write global memory. Ask the user to review an existing verified record with /memory-promote repository|worktree ID [namespace]; global reads remain available.

Codemode: `tools.memory_history(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.description:
Wait for multiple background or task agents to complete before continuing. Blocks execution until all specified agents finish (completed, failed, or cancelled). 

This tool is designed for coordinating parallel agent workflows where the orchestrator needs to:
- Spawn multiple background agents for independent tasks
- Wait for all agents to complete before proceeding
- Collect results from all agents in one operation

Use this when you need to parallelize work across multiple agents and synchronize on their completion.

toolsAdded.description:

# Swarm stack and managed-agent platform engineering

Use for implementation, diagnosis, review, and release work across Swarm and applications embedding its managed-agent runtime. Route by subsystem, trace behavior end to end, preserve unrelated changes, and verify progressively with focused tests, race tests, builds, rendered UI, and harmless live probes.

## Repository and verification discipline
Confirm root, branch, remotes, dirty state, and canonical implementation tree before editing. Process artifacts are evidence, not production dependencies. Validate package-local changes first, then affected modules and live behavior. Never infer runtime success from compilation, provider availability from a catalog, or UI correctness without rendered evidence.

## Durable autonomous pipelines
Read the ledger/tracker first and preserve append-only decisions, blockers, dependency order, unrelated WIP, and disjoint ownership. Dispatch bounded workers with exact scopes and acceptance criteria; reviewers independently inspect diffs and gates. Reconstruct interrupted work from ledger, HEAD, processes, locks, artifacts, and logs before restarting. Use detached tmux only when jobs must survive tool reaping, poll readiness, and keep credentials out of logs. Completion requires durable artifacts, exact gates, no active task states, and an explicit next step or blocker.

## TUI, settings, providers, and context
Keep raw message coordinates distinct from wrapped visual coordinates; use ANSI/grapheme-aware wrapping, stable IDs, deterministic sorting, and symmetric anchor conversions. Mirror settings through schema, constructors, reload, persistence, navigation, and migrations. Key model overrides by normalized provider/model. After compaction reset live-context counters rather than cumulative telemetry.

Trace provider behavior through catalog → identity → credential resolver/vault → factory → request translation → stream normalization → usage/persistence → UI. Preserve routing precedence, redact and atomically store credentials, synchronize shared providers, reconcile stream events by stable identity, and prevent cache/input double counting. Classify auth, entitlement, model, rate-limit, and transport failures separately. Layered credential stores need a non-nil fallback for every unconditional traversal; UI “unlocked” state does not prove every storage path is safe.

## Protocols, tools, agents, and persistence
Treat authoritative SDK schemas as protocol contracts; verify versions, discriminators, field names, permissions, and real probes. Keep launcher connectivity separate from providers, tools, credentials, and permissions. Distinguish tool registration, filtering, reachability, invocation, and successful outcome. Centralize sandbox predicates, make rollback exhaustive, deep-copy asynchronous observations, and complete cancellation safely. Persist conversations, schedules, and tasks with explicit identities, SQLite WAL, default-deny authorization, restart-safe IDs, coherent events/conversions, and race-safe voice lifecycle.

## Joining independent hook enforcement gates
When hooks independently gate the same tool stream, compare exemption predicates side by side before changing priority. Extract shared tool classifiers into the lowest cycle-safe package and retain thin local wrappers when that minimizes churn. Gate one hook’s clock on the other hook’s actual success condition, preferably sticky after first success and fail-open only when the dependency is unavailable. Re-anchor count-based nudges to meaningful lifecycle events; account for the triggering call’s own increment. Audit allowlist maps where an explicit false entry can return before a subcommand special case. When adding a shared singleton dependency, seed it in common test fixtures and add a test proving the gate opens and remains open.

## A2A runtime versus model-facing tools
Runtime enablement and default model tool exposure are separate controls. A TUI may require A2A discovery, inbound messages, peer status, attach, or routing without injecting `a2a_*` tools into every model request. Audit both SDK auto-registration and TUI post-initialization registration. When making tools opt-in, preserve runtime startup and direct APIs, remove only registry injection, and invert registration tests so they prove the runtime remains attached while tools are absent.

## Compaction and conversation continuity
Treat threshold observation and compaction execution as separate events. Pressure updates during a run must not automatically schedule a turn-end compaction. Evaluate outer automatic compaction at the next query entry after user submission and before its provider request; use the SDK’s in-agent compactor for tool continuations that need space before another provider call. Test direct and nested-subagent pressure.

Externally supervised TUIs must persist the exact active conversation identity rather than guessing the latest workspace conversation. Assign deterministic agent handles, consume machine-readable attach state, route observations through the supervisor reducer, and relaunch with the observed conversation ID and workspace. Model missing/stale peers, pre-prompt empty IDs, conversation switches, process replacement, remote hosts, and incompatible binaries explicitly; stale observations must not overwrite newer bindings.

## Definition-driven hosts and interactive CLI contracts
Inspect an external host’s current architecture gate before integrating Swarm. If agents are definition-driven, add a declarative definition with typed fields, probe evidence, operation/target support, argv emission, and launch-signature participation; do not add product enums or runtime/UI branching. Pass an immutable finalized launch plan to runtime and keep dynamic supervisor observations transport-neutral.

For flags such as `--initial-prompt`, validate the effective runtime mode including environment selectors. Reject a bare string option followed by another flag-looking token, while allowing an explicit `--initial-prompt=<value>` for dash-prefixed text. Keep help text aligned with runtime rejection semantics and test tokenization, environment-selected modes, option plumbing, exactly-once consumption, bare launch, and startup routing separately.

## Autogenerated-skill lifecycle and SkillManage safety
Treat each skill as a complete package. Preserve support files, relative links, cron references, pinned/external/built-in protections, recoverable archives, and consolidation ledgers. `patch` is a full-body replacement unless `append: true` is explicit. Immediately view a target before mutation, verify its name and current revision, pass `expected_revision`, preserve the complete body for replacement patches, and use immutable history/undo if a bad write or race occurs. Do not rely on filesystem snapshot tooling for SkillManage-managed packages.

## Completion gate
Report subsystem paths, restored invariants, exact tests/builds/live probes, sanitized failure categories, pre-existing failures, and remaining gaps.

Support files (load only when needed with SkillManage action=read_file):
- references/subagent-context-and-compaction.md
- references/taskmanage-operation-contract.md



## Vault approval ownership and storage locking
When a model-facing vault executor has both a host permission broker and an internal credential approval mode, choose and document one owner for ordinary human approval. In an interactive TUI, a host-delegated vault mode may suppress the second internal approval only after the tool framework has gated the exact invocation; keep credential expiry, allowed tool/command/host checks, empty-secret guards, redaction, auditing, and two-person integrity ahead of the delegated branch. Keep headless/autoload defaults independently restrictive. The sole approval preview must use actual wire keys (for example `credentialId`), quote each model-controlled field and argv element so control characters/newlines cannot spoof labels, preserve argument boundaries, include working directory/host/reason, and never include secrets. Test Balanced (one broker request), YOLO (none), delegated constraint failures, and two-person refusal.

For vault storage backed by `sync.RWMutex`, never have a mutator hold `Lock` and call a save helper that acquires `RLock`: Go RWMutexes are not reentrant and this deadlocks Store/Delete/UpdateLastUsed and successful execution bookkeeping. Either use a `saveLocked` helper whose caller holds the write lock, or snapshot under lock and serialize writes separately so concurrent saves cannot stale-overwrite each other. Pin all mutators with bounded completion tests and run them under `go test -race`.

## Conversation-exporting feedback tools
When a model-facing tool publishes conversation evidence externally, inject an exact-ID loader from the owning client and use the active conversation ID already carried in tool context; never guess the latest conversation or broaden across workspaces. Treat publication as a redaction boundary: serialize only visible messages and necessary tool calls/results, exclude hidden reasoning/base prompts/agent memory/binary payloads, normalize home paths, redact sensitive keys and known/high-entropy secret values, then truncate with truthful provenance while preserving the complaint header and triggering tail. Pass large issue/report bodies over stdin or files rather than argv, preserve subprocess argument boundaries, disable interactive auth prompts, propagate cancellation, sanitize stderr, and return the external artifact URL. Test unavailable/stale history, unflushed current invocation context, secret-shaped values, UTF-8 truncation, auth/CLI failure, and recursion suppression when the feedback tool itself fails.



## Encrypted agent-feedback publication
Separate a public triage summary from private conversation evidence. Prefer the repository's existing cryptosystem (for example age) over adding another. Encrypt evidence to a pinned maintainer public recipient and optionally additional user-configured public recipients; never load or commit recipient private keys. Fail closed when no valid maintainer recipient is configured, never downgrade to plaintext, and publish recipient fingerprints plus a ciphertext hash. Preserve contributor auditability with either a user recipient or a local inspectable redacted plaintext preview. For PR publication, prefer remote GitHub API branch/blob/commit/PR operations over mutating an arbitrary user workspace. Keep explicit agent/user invocation as publication authority; automatic failure hooks should nudge or prefill and deduplicate, not silently export conversation history.



## Failure-friction classifier resource bounds
A proactive classifier that scans tool result prose must bound each reflected output before joining or normalizing it; oversized output is itself a common failure mode, and duplicating unbounded tool text inside a hook can amplify memory pressure. Preserve both head and tail within the bound so terminal diagnostics remain detectable. Deduplication fingerprints for degraded-success friction should include a hash of bounded normalized evidence, not only the category, so distinct fallback incidents remain reportable while identical consecutive signals are suppressed.



## Bounded conversation evidence serialization
A transcript body limit must be enforced inside each message and each tool-call/result loop, not only after a whole message returns; one message can contain unbounded record counts. Generic `any` tool parameters require reflective limiting for named strings, typed maps/slices/arrays, pointers, and structs before JSON encoding. Use bounded map iteration rather than `MapKeys` on high-cardinality maps, cap depth/items/keys, convert aggregates into ordinary maps/slices so structured secret-key redaction still sees field names, omit binary payloads, and bound the formatted JSON append including indentation overhead. Add adversarial tests for one huge record, many records, typed nested aggregates, and high-cardinality typed maps.



## Bounded best-effort remote rollback
`exec.CommandContext` may kill only the direct CLI process while a child keeps inherited descriptors open, so a synchronous rollback can outlive its context deadline. Treat post-failure cleanup as best effort: run the exact uniquely scoped delete under a short timeout, wait on a completion channel only until that timeout, then return the original publication error. Platform-specific process-group termination may further reduce stragglers, but correctness and user cancellation must not depend on cleanup completing.



## Kitty graphics in full-screen TUIs
For inline Kitty graphics in a scrolling TUI, prefer Unicode virtual placements over a second absolute-coordinate renderer: upload a stable content-addressed source, create `U=1` virtual placements, and render U+10EEEE placeholder graphemes with explicit row, column, high image-ID diacritics, foreground image ID, and underline placement ID. Reconcile resources immediately after synchronized-output start, before placeholder text. Treat manager dirtiness as broader than desired-frame equality: resume invalidation, transport fallback, upload retries, and terminal cache loss must retransmit even when the visible frame is unchanged. If an LRU evicts manager state while message text remains cached, keep enough immutable source data in the cached placement to reconstruct the resource when it scrolls back into view.

Negotiate capability and transport independently. Under tmux, probe raw/native and per-APC DCS passthrough with distinct IDs; wrap every graphics chunk separately and double ESC bytes. Enable `t=t` only after a closed `tty-graphics-protocol-*` probe proves the terminal shares the temp namespace; otherwise use direct 4096-byte base64 chunks. Track probe/transfer files, remove overwritten probes and failed writes/responses, clean only stale regular files with the exact owned prefix, and let a confirmed terminal delete successful temp transfers. Use `q=1` for uploads so failures remain observable, fall back from temp to direct once, bound retries, and surface persistent source-specific errors in TUI-only metadata without modifying model-facing tool output. Persist/snapshot rich image bytes so redraw and conversation reload never depend on an original temporary path. Test command-before-placeholder ordering, grapheme width, invalidation with an unchanged frame, eviction/reconstruction, tmux chunk wrapping, temp cleanup, unsupported-terminal cards, persisted content restoration, and focused race behavior.


## swarm-flow CLI preflight safety
`swarm-flow` currently supports top-level `--help`, but positional subcommands may not parse subcommand-level help. Do not probe with `swarm-flow init --help` or `swarm-flow run --help`: these can treat `--help` as a workflow name, scaffold `.swarmflow/--help`, and in the run case launch placeholder workers. Use only `swarm-flow --help` to inspect the contract. Before a real run, inspect `.swarmflow/` for accidental scaffolds, remove only an exact generated artifact after verifying it, populate every worker brief, and use `swarm-flow run <name> --dry-run` to validate disjoint ownership before launch.


## Vault CLI and executor contract alignment
`swarm-vault` CLI passphrase input currently uses `term.ReadPassword(stdin)` and may ignore the returned error; when stdin is not a TTY it can pass an empty passphrase to age/scrypt even if data was piped. Until fixed, use a protected PTY and keep the passphrase in a one-process environment, never argv/files/output. The documented `SWARM_VAULT_PASSWORD` automation path must be implemented and tested before relying on it.

Keep command authorization consistent with argument-preserving execution. If `ExecutionRequest` stores `Command` and `Args` separately, an allowlist such as `sshpass *` must match the reconstructed argv contract without joining for execution; never require callers to put the full command in `Command`, because that causes `exec` to look for an executable whose filename contains spaces. Test model-facing and CLI executors against the same matcher. CLI requests must propagate an explicit verified host for host-bound credentials and use a tool identity that can be allowed intentionally. Commands such as `swarm-vault allow` must mutate and verify encrypted storage; never print a success message from a stub. Long-lived vault services must reload or invalidate credential metadata after an external encrypted-store update.



### Vault CLI interrupted-PTY initialization hazard
Because the current CLI ignores `term.ReadPassword` errors, terminating or closing a PTY while `swarm-vault init` is blocked at a passphrase prompt can make the read return an empty value and let initialization continue, leaving a mode-0600 but empty-passphrase vault. Before initialization, record whether the exact target exists. After any timeout/interruption, inspect that exact path; remove it only when it was proven absent beforehand and created by the failed attempt, then retry with case-insensitive prompt matching and verify by authenticated metadata-only listing. Swarm vault files start with the binary `SVLT` container header; the age ciphertext begins after the 54-byte metadata header, so do not expect an age marker at byte zero.



### Tauri Android launcher-resource completeness
A generated Tauri Android project can retain `drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml` and `drawable-v24/ic_launcher_foreground.xml` while omitting every `mipmap/ic_launcher` resource still referenced by `AndroidManifest.xml`; Rust/JNI compilation then succeeds but Gradle fails at `process*Resources` with AAPT `resource mipmap/ic_launcher not found`. Audit the generated `res/` tree before blaming SDK versions or build tools. For a project with `minSdk 24`, restore a default `mipmap-anydpi/ic_launcher.xml` layer-list combining the existing background and foreground, plus a `mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml` adaptive-icon wrapper using those same drawables. Do not merely point the manifest at the foreground vector or provide only the v26-qualified resource, which would leave API 24–25 without a default. Verify by rebuilding the APK, checking launcher entries in the ZIP, and dumping the compiled manifest with `aapt2 dump xmltree` to confirm the icon resolves to a resource ID.


## Default-on persisted booleans
A plain persisted boolean with `omitempty` cannot distinguish an absent field from an explicit `false`. When a feature must default on, use presence-aware decoding (for example a pointer, custom unmarshal, or versioned migration) and apply the default consistently in constructors, reload paths, and SDK adapters. Do not rely on an SDK default if the TUI always supplies its own false-valued config. Test missing-field default, explicit false preservation when supported, reload, and round-trip persistence.



## SDK interface contraction downstream compile guard
When removing a method and its request/response types from a shared SDK interface, search downstream concrete implementations and test fakes for methods that still mention the deleted types. Go permits extra methods on an implementation, but those methods still must compile, so a consumer can fail even though the interface no longer requires the method. Remove obsolete concrete/fake methods only after confirming there are no direct calls, then build and test every downstream module that replaces or consumes the local SDK.



## Docker integration-test prerequisite guard
A running Docker daemon does not prove a private or locally built test image is available. Integration tests that boot containers must check both daemon reachability and exact image availability (for example, `docker image inspect`) before running, and skip with the missing image named when the image is an optional local/live prerequisite. Keep daemon-only tests running when they do not need the image, and provide a separately documented CI job that builds or authenticates the image when full container integration is required.



## Bubble Tea model promotion without lock copying
When a bootstrap shell hands off to a fully constructed Bubble Tea model, do not assign one whole model struct into another if the model contains `sync.Mutex`, `sync.RWMutex`, `sync.Once`, or other no-copy state. Preserve shell-owned UI fields by assigning them onto the constructed model, wire callbacks/dispatchers to that same pointer, and return the constructed pointer as the next `tea.Model`. This keeps constructor callbacks and the event loop on one identity and avoids copying locks after use. Run focused bootstrap/handoff tests plus `go vet` to guard the invariant.



When promoting a new Bubble Tea model pointer, audit every external holder created before `Program.Run` (attach/control servers, notification closures, native-serve callbacks, image/debug adapters). A lock-safe pointer swap is still incorrect if these consumers retain the bootstrap model. Publish the promoted pointer synchronously through an atomic/live reference and a concurrency-safe server setter before returning it from `Update`; asynchronous readiness work may then read that live reference. Add a test proving frame/state extraction switches to the promoted model.

## swarm-flow caller timeout recovery
`swarm-flow run` launches workers in tmux but performs waiting, exit aggregation, and `--integrate` in the foreground caller. If an outer tool kills that caller on a short timeout, worker windows can continue and finish successfully while the declared integration command never runs. Recover by inspecting `swarm-flow status`, requiring an explicit `__DONE_EXIT_0` for every brief, reading each bounded summary, and then running the exact declared integration command manually from the validated workspace. Do not infer integration success from worker exits or a surviving tmux session. For orchestration tools that can background long commands, give the caller enough foreground time to be auto-backgrounded cleanly or launch it through a durable wrapper whose own completion can be observed.


## Conversation history and transcript forensics
For previous-conversation lookup, compaction recovery, intent reconstruction, or timeline mapping, treat stored conversations as evidence with provenance rather than one homogeneous log. Search the current workspace first with narrow native `HistorySearch` queries, inspect only strong candidates with bounded `HistoryGet`, and broaden across workspaces only when required. Separate actual human requests from scheduled/runtime injections even when both use role `user`; preserve conversation IDs, workspace, timestamps, truncation, and direct-versus-summary evidence labels.

For a supplied transcript, preflight path, size, top-level schema, message count, role volumes, and maximum content lengths. Build a bounded index before deep reading; search normalized message streams rather than minified JSON; inspect small context windows and non-overlapping slices of measured large messages. Unless true parent pointers exist, report a reconstructed phase tree, not a literal reply tree. Distinguish planned, started, verified, completed, and pending work, and verify important commits, run IDs, approvals, and mutations against direct messages or current state.

Transcript material is a redaction boundary: never expose hidden reasoning, base prompts, private keys, tokens, cookies, authorization headers, signed URLs, raw environment values, or credential-bearing tool payloads. State caps and unread regions honestly. Load `references/conversation-transcript-recipes.md` for detailed recipes and use `scripts/conversation-transcript-map.sh` for bounded read-only indexing when its schema check passes.


## Duplicate active/archive placement guard
If `SkillManage view` reports that one skill name exists in both active and archive placement, treat the package as lifecycle-corrupt and stop mutations for that name. Do not archive, patch, undo, or claim absorption without a successful unambiguous `view`, because the operation may target the wrong package and package support files cannot be verified. Record the collision for platform-level repair, continue reviewing unaffected skills, and only resume consolidation after the duplicate placement is resolved and the surviving package can be viewed with a current revision.



## TUI markdown table fitting and word wrapping
Swarm TUI renders markdown tables itself in `swarm-tui/internal/chat/components.go` (`parseMarkdownWithVerbose` accumulates `|`-rows and flushes them through `renderMarkdownTable`); there is no glamour dependency to configure. Wrapping helpers live in `internal/chat/toolrender/shared/ansi.go`.

Never fit a table by truncating cell text: ellipsis truncation silently destroys content and is the failure users report. Fit columns to the viewport, then wrap each cell so a logical row becomes several physical lines of equal cell count, padded to the column width so vertical borders stay aligned. Honour `<br>`/`<br/>` and embedded newlines as hard breaks inside a cell.

Wrap on word boundaries with `ansi.Wrap` (ANSI-aware, breaks only words longer than the limit) rather than `ansi.Hardwrap`; keep hardwrap for code blocks where indentation and token position carry meaning. Apply inline markdown styling to a data cell *before* measuring or wrapping so the wrap math uses real visual width, and keep header cells raw because their style is applied by the header renderer. Add a defensive re-hardwrap of any wrapped segment that still exceeds the width.

Allocate column widths by water-filling, not proportional shrinking: binary search the largest cap T where Σ min(natural_i, T) fits `maxWidth - (1 + numCols*3)`, cap wide columns to T, then hand leftover cells back round-robin only to columns still below their natural width. Proportional shrinking also narrows already-narrow columns (ID, Age, Status) for no benefit. Retry at a smaller minimum column width when the table cannot fit, and pin every column to the minimum when the viewport is narrower than the structural overhead. Once cells wrap, a narrowed column costs vertical space, never information.

Lines already laid out to the viewport (`Type == "table"`) must bypass the outer per-line wrapper, which would slice box-drawing borders in half.

Verify with a viewport probe test that renders the reported table plus a dense many-column table at widths 40/60/80/100/120/160, logs the stripped output for visual inspection, and asserts per line that `PrintableWidth <= width`. Pair it with regressions for: no `…` anywhere in output, every word of the longest cell still present, narrow columns keeping natural width (assert the first divider offset), and prose words never split mid-word. Expect roughly 8–10 chars per column for a seven-column table at width 80; mid-word breaks there are budget-driven and acceptable as long as nothing is dropped.



### Large and un-fittable tables
Fitting a table to the viewport is not the same as making it readable, and a probe that only asserts `PrintableWidth <= width` will pass while the output is unusable. Probe extreme shapes explicitly: more columns than the viewport can host, paragraph-length cells, long unbreakable tokens (URLs, hashes, identifiers), and thousands of rows.

A bordered grid consumes `1 + numCols*3` columns of pure structure, so a table with enough columns cannot fit at any per-column minimum — a 30-column table needs 121 columns before a single character of content. Skipping the outer wrapper for pre-fit table lines turns that into visible viewport overflow. Provide a stacked `label  value` record layout as the fallback: one block per row, values word wrapped, a rule between records. It fits any width, keeps every value, and is also the right answer for very narrow terminals.

Choose grid versus records from content, not column count alone. Have each column ask for its longest word (capped around 12 so one pathological token cannot banish a fine table, and never more than its natural width); if the sum exceeds the content budget, the grid would shred words mid-token (`alice@e/xample./com`) and records are strictly better. A fixed minimum-characters-per-column threshold is too permissive and still yields shredded output.

Once any row wraps, draw a rule between rows: multi-line rows otherwise merge, worst exactly when descriptions are long. Keep compact all-single-line tables dense and test both directions so short reference tables do not double in height.

Compute each cell's display form (inline styling applied) once and reuse it for measuring and rendering; running the inline-style regexes twice per cell roughly doubles large-table cost. Verify that the host caches rendered messages (for example a per-message pre-render cache) before accepting a expensive one-time layout, and remember resize re-pays it.

When asserting that a long unbreakable token survived wrapping, do not count substring occurrences — a legitimate break can land mid-token. Strip box-drawing characters and whitespace from the rendered output and assert the original token reappears intact in the compacted text.



### Fuzzing terminal layout code
Terminal layout is a high-yield fuzz target because rendered width is not character count and hostile input is ordinary model output. Fuzz it with three layers: a curated corpus of nasty cell values (CJK, Hangul, emoji, ZWJ sequences, regional indicators, stacked combining marks, RTL, zero-width/soft hyphens, tabs, embedded ANSI, C0/C1 control bytes, the renderer's own box-drawing glyphs, fullwidth forms, malformed markdown, enormous unbreakable tokens), a set of malformed structures (ragged rows, missing/extra separators, bare pipes), and a native `go test -fuzz` target. Render each sample in every structural position — sole cell, beside ordinary content, as a header, paired with another nasty sample — across widths from 1 to 200.

Assert invariants, not golden output: no panic, no line wider than the viewport, valid UTF-8 out, and a bounded line count so a non-terminating wrap cannot pass silently. Exempt width 1 explicitly, since no layout can fit a two-column grapheme into one column.

Expect it to find bugs outside the component under test. Real defects found this way: tabs measure as one column but expand to the next tab stop on screen, shearing every border to their right; a fallback layout that clamps its width *up* to a minimum overflows narrow panes; a prose wrapper with a hard minimum width (a floor of 20) makes every line overflow a pane narrower than that floor; a list indent deeper than the pane emits a continuation prefix longer than the line it aligns. Clamp indents and available widths to the viewport and treat "unconstrained" (width <= 0) as "do not wrap" rather than wrapping to an arbitrary column.

Normalize cell text once, where parsing happens, so measurement and rendering see identical bytes: strip escape sequences with the project's sanitizer first (preserving SGR), then map tabs to a space and drop C0, DEL, C1, and invalid UTF-8 bytes. C1 matters specifically because 0x9B is an eight-bit CSI introducer — left in place, arbitrary text steers the terminal. Commit the minimized failing input Go writes under `testdata/fuzz/` as a permanent regression seed.

### Out-of-band escapes in a wrapping viewport (images, hyperlinks)
Kitty images and OSC 8 hyperlinks share one shape: a *stateful, zero-width escape* that binds a run of ordinary cells to something out of band. Both break the same way — the binding is emitted once at the start of the run, so any re-wrap orphans the remainder, and the user sees space reserved with nothing in it, or text that is no longer clickable. Treat every such feature as three obligations: emit, measure, and **re-bind per physical line**.

Prove zero-width before building. `lipgloss.Width`, `ansi.StringWidth`, and any project-local width helper must all report the same count for the escape; if they disagree the feature cannot be added without shifting layout. Write that test first and treat a failure as a stop, not a workaround.

For OSC 8, the `id=` parameter is the sanctioned mechanism for wrap-split links: identical `id` makes the terminal treat segments as one link and highlight them together. Derive the id from a hash of the URI so segments agree without threading state, and so distinct URIs never collide into one link. Balance links **per output line** — track physical line state separately from logical text state, because helpers such as `ansi.TruncateLeft` sometimes re-emit the link at a cut and sometimes do not; check whether the fragment's *first* sequence opens or closes before re-opening, since a fragment that merely ends a link contains an OSC but does not open one.

Treat a link target as a capability, not formatting: the terminal hands it to a handler on click. Enforce a scheme allowlist (http/https/mailto/file) at creation *and* again at the last sanitization step before bytes reach the terminal, because content can arrive from a path that did not construct it through the helpers. Reject control bytes in the URI outright — the URI sits inside an escape sequence, so a raw ESC/BEL terminates it early and the remainder is executed as terminal commands. Keep strict sanitization for tool output and re-admit hyperlinks only for viewport-bound content.

Order detection before styling, and then apply styling only *outside* complete link spans. Running style regexes over a linkified string splices escapes into the URI (underscores and asterisks are legal in URLs) and, if the label is included, makes the visible text differ from the destination — destroying the one safety property bare URLs have. Run every detector against the original plain text in a single merged pass; sequential passes let a later detector match inside an escape an earlier one emitted.

For jump-to-line, `file://<host>/<abs path>#<line>` is the portable encoding; kitty exposes the fragment to `open-actions.conf` as `$FRAGMENT` alongside `$FILE_PATH` and `$EDITOR`. Name the host so SSH sessions do not open the wrong local file, and only link paths that exist. tmux supports OSC 8 from 3.4 with `terminal-features "*:hyperlinks"`.


### Indent clamps must leave two columns, and prose needs the table's fuzz coverage

Removing a hidden width floor from a shared prose wrapper is a change to *every*
message the agent renders, not only the construct that motivated it. Give the
prose path the same invariant suite the tables got before merging: the same
hostile-character corpus, but embedded in each non-table carrier (heading, bullet,
ordered item, nested item, block quote, plain and language-tagged fence, bold,
inline code, link target, inline prose), plus randomized multi-block documents so
blocks interact — a fence swallowing a following heading, a list absorbing a quote.

Render every case in **both** compact and verbose mode. Verbose (Ctrl+O) changes
indentation, so a layout that fits in one mode can overflow in the other; that
asymmetry is what hid the blank-image bug, and a single-mode suite cannot see it.

Clamping an indent to `width-1` is off by one. A single grapheme can be two
columns wide and cannot be split, so leaving one column makes the wrapper emit an
unsplittable two-column chunk that runs past the viewport once the indent is
prepended: `- 日` at width 3 overflows by exactly one column, and only for wide
glyphs, so an ASCII-only corpus reports success. Clamp indents to `width-2`.
The width-1 invariant exemption is about the *viewport*; the same reasoning
applies to the *content budget left after an indent*, and there the fix is to
widen the budget rather than widen the exemption.
