toolsAdded.name: memory_history
toolsAdded.description:
Recall and enrich durable redacted memory. Use operation=ask with a natural-language query to have a read-only memory agent answer using cited scoped records; no evidence yields no answer. Use operation=recall to retrieve source cards without an answer. To pass an explicit 'remember that' request to the memory reviewer, use operation=offer with text, source and cited evidence in repository/worktree scope; it stores only a candidate and acknowledges indexing. Memory records what is known: project architecture, domain facts, terminology, decisions and rationale, constraints, preferences, and relevant ongoing context. A project's established process is knowledge about that project. Reusable instructions for how an agent should investigate, implement, debug, or verify belong in skills, not memory. Separate factual context from procedural advice when an observation contains both. Preserve evidence, uncertainty, and freshness; later corrections may invalidate earlier claims. Do not treat an agent's success claim as verified fact. Use repository scope for shared project knowledge; worktree scope for unmerged or experimental facts; session scope for local conversational context. Use global only for explicitly shareable cross-project facts or preferences, not merely because a lesson sounds reusable. Do not duplicate a fact into both repository and global scope by default. Reading combined scopes does not authorize wider writes. Search before saving to avoid duplicates. Include evidence references; exclude secrets and raw transcripts. Defaults to repository scope. Search scope all includes repository/worktree/global. Use search with status candidate to find pending knowledge, then get by id to inspect its full evidence. Review source evidence and later corrections before using correct to mark a candidate verified; leave unsupported claims pending. Writes default to candidate; verified records require evidence references (verification is an attributed claim, not automatic proof). correct/delete require id and expectedRevision. Agent tool calls cannot write global memory. Ask the user to review an existing verified record with /memory-promote repository|worktree ID [namespace]; global reads remain available.

Codemode: `tools.memory_history(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: multi_agent_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for multiple background or task agents to complete before continuing. Blocks execution until all specified agents finish (completed, failed, or cancelled). 

This tool is designed for coordinating parallel agent workflows where the orchestrator needs to:
- Spawn multiple background agents for independent tasks
- Wait for all agents to complete before proceeding
- Collect results from all agents in one operation

Use this when you need to parallelize work across multiple agents and synchronize on their completion.

Codemode: `tools.multi_agent_wait(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: scheduler
toolsAdded.description:

toolsAdded.description:
Manage stored connection and authentication entries for autonomous work. Use action=list with optional query, kind, scope, or tags to find an entry, action=get to retrieve one, action=add to store one, and action=remove to delete one. The transparent vault returns retrieved secrets in plaintext; use them only for the current task and never echo, quote, log, commit, or expose them. Use action=remove only when requested.

action.description: Use get for one credential, list to discover available credentials, add to store a credential, or remove to delete one.

id.description: Credential identifier. Required for get and remove; use the id returned by list.

kind.description: Credential kind, such as password, api_key, or ssh_key.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive search across credential id, name, and kind. Prefer query/list before asking the user to provide a credential.

tags.description: Optional tags that every result must contain.

cursor.description: Cursor returned by a previous list operation.

details.description: Include nonessential metadata such as tags and allowed hosts.

secret.description: Credential value to store. The vault is transparent and returns secrets in plaintext for get; never echo, log, commit, or expose retrieved secrets.

target.description: Optional environment variable or file target associated with this entry.

export function resolveToolEvidence(reference: string, sessionManager: EvidenceSessionManager | undefined, aliases: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {}): boolean {
  const match = /^tool:([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)(?:#(\d+))?$/i.exec(reference.trim());
  if (!match || !sessionManager) return false;
  let name = match[1];
  const names = sessionResultNames(sessionManager);
  if (!names.includes(name) && aliases[name]) {
    const targets = [...new Set(aliases[name])];
    if (targets.length !== 1) return false;
    name = targets[0];
  }
  const count = names.filter(value => value === name).length;
  if (!match[2]) return count > 0;
  const index = Number(match[2]);
  return index >= 1 && index <= count;
}

export function registerTaskManage(pi: { registerTool(tool: unknown): void; appendEntry(type: string, data: unknown): void; on(event: string, handler: (event: unknown, ctx: {sessionManager?: {getEntries(): readonly unknown[]; getBranch?(): readonly unknown[]}; ui?: {setWidget(key: string, content: unknown): void}})=>void): void }, presentation = taskManageRenderers, options: TaskManagerOptions = {}): TaskManager {
  options = { ...options }; // Each registration owns its defaults and session closures.
  const manager = new TaskManager(
    entry => pi.appendEntry(entry.type, entry.data),
    event => pi.appendEntry(event.type, event.data),
    options,
  );
  let ui: {setWidget(key: string, content: unknown): void} | undefined;
  let sessionManager: EvidenceSessionManager | undefined;
  const refreshWidget = (ctx?: {ui?: {setWidget(key: string, content: unknown): void}}) => {
    ui = ctx?.ui ?? ui;
    if (!ui) return;
    const tasks = manager.snapshot().tasks.filter(task => task.status !== "deleted");
    const visible = tasks.some(task => task.status === "pending" || task.status === "in_progress");
    ui.setWidget("swarm-tasks", visible
      ? ((_tui: unknown, theme: RenderTheme) => taskWidgetRenderer(tasks, theme))
      : undefined);
  };
  const bindSession = (_event: unknown, ctx: EvidenceContext) => {
    sessionManager = ctx.sessionManager;
    manager.rehydrate((ctx.sessionManager?.getBranch?.() ?? ctx.sessionManager?.getEntries() ?? []) as JournalEntry[]);
    refreshWidget(ctx);
  };
  pi.on("session_start", bindSession);
  pi.on("session_switch", bindSession);
  options.sessionEvidenceHints ??= () => {
    const counts = new Map<string, number>();
    for (const name of sessionResultNames(sessionManager)) {
      if (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(name)) counts.set(name, (counts.get(name) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
    return counts.size ? `; available: ${[...counts].slice(0, 8).map(([name, count]) => `tool:${name}#${count}`).join(", ")}` : "; no tool results on the current branch";
  };
  // Persist canonical names so later alias configuration cannot retarget saved answers.
  options.canonicalizeToolEvidence ??= reference => {
    const match = /^tool:([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)(#\d+)?$/i.exec(reference.trim());
    if (!match || !sessionManager) return reference;
    if (resolveToolEvidence(reference, sessionManager)) return reference;
    const targets = [...new Set(options.toolAliases?.[match[1]] ?? [])];
    if (targets.length !== 1 || !resolveToolEvidence(reference, sessionManager, options.toolAliases)) return reference;
    return `tool:${targets[0]}${match[2] ?? ""}`;
  };
  // Intentionally exact-only here: supplied aliases are canonicalized above.
  // Retained aliases have no historical mapping provenance; resolving them
  // with today's alias map could silently retarget already-saved evidence.
  options.resolveSessionEvidence ??= reference => resolveToolEvidence(reference, sessionManager);
  pi.registerTool({ name:"TaskManage", label:"Manage tasks", description:"Manage ordered tasks. ## Outcome

The rejection happened because `tool:mcp__Bash` names a tool that doesn't exist in this session. The resolver matches the tool name exactly against recorded tool results, and the native shell tool is recorded as `Bash`. The correct form is `tool:Bash#<n>`, where `<n>` is a 1-based position among `Bash` results on the current session branch. No files were modified in this turn.

## Evidence

- `packages/tools/taskmanage/src/task-manage.ts:700` emits the error. For any `tool:` ref it sets `tool_result_unavailable: use an exact registered tool name and a current-branch result index`, appends the session hints, and returns `resolveSessionEvidence(reference)`.
- `task-manage.ts:686` turns that failure into `validation_failed` for the completion call.
- `task-manage.ts:1078` parses the ref with `/^tool:([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)(?:#(\d+))?$/i`. `mcp__Bash` matches this pattern, so the syntax itself is accepted. The failure is in the lookup.
- `task-manage.ts:1071-1074` collects names from session entries, keeping only `message` entries with `role === "toolResult"`, using `toolName`. There is no `isError` filter, so failed calls count.
- `task-manage.ts:1082` checks `names.includes(name)`, which is case-sensitive. The `/i` flag on the regex does not make the lookup case-insensitive.
- `task-manage.ts:1087-1090` counts matches for `name`. With `#n`, it requires `1 <= n <= count`. So `#3` is 1-based.
- `task-manage.ts:1118-1125` builds the hint list in the form `tool:<name>#<count>`. This is the source of the "available" list in the error.
- `task-manage.ts:1137` wires the resolver to the current session manager.
- `packages/tools/mcp/src/index.ts:69` shows MCP tools are registered as `mcp__${id}__${t.name}`. `mcp__Bash` would require an MCP server with id `Bash`, which this session does not show.

## Analysis

Observed facts:
- The resolver is exact-name and 1-based, and it counts failed results.
- The native tool is listed as `Bash` in this session's capabilities (lowercase `bash` in the summary, `Bash` in the tool results I received).

Interpretation:
- The most likely root cause is the wrong tool name: `mcp__Bash` was used where `Bash` is the recorded name.
- Alternative causes I could not rule out from here: the `#3` index may exceed the number of `Bash` results on the current branch, or a compaction may have changed what the branch contains. Both would show up in the hint list in the rejection message. I did not read the live session log, so I cannot confirm which `Bash` results are on the branch.
